Overview:

Quality Control and Normalization

  1. Step 1: Load data and meta data
    Load data and meta data and filter out any QC samples.
  2. Step 2: Filter low count samples
    Inspect quality control samples by plotting
  3. Step 3: Taxonomical-filtering
    Identify treshold for low abundant taxa to filter
    1. Split clade name into seperate columns
    2. Identify the strains to remove
    3. Aggregate removed strains by higher levels
    4. Get longer format and add back clade_names
    5. Subtract filtered taxa from each higher taxa levels
    6. Check for samples with total taxa < 60% after filtering
    7. Check and replace negative values with zero
    8. Re-normalize each sample to 100%
  4. Step 4: Simplify clade names
  5. Step 5: Plot barplots
  6. Step 6: Centered Log Ratio (CLR) Transformation
  7. Step 7: Exploratory Unsupervised PCA
  8. Step 8: Exploratory Heatmap

g <- c(
  "0" = "0-1",
  "1" = "0-1",
  "2" = "2-3",
  "3" = "2-3",
  "4" = "4-5",
  "5" = "4-5"
)

gr_data <- meta_data %>%
  rename(
    `Symptom score (0-5)` = "Symptom score (0-5) - ibland har de svarat olika skriftligt i frågeformuläret och muntligt vid inklusiion, då har jag valt den högsta scoren"
  ) %>%
  select(
    svamp_ID,
    `Clinical score (0-5)`,
    `Fungal culture: C. albicans (y/n)`,
    `Fungal culture: Non-albicans candida spp. (y/n)`,
    `Symptom score (0-5)`,
    `Recurring fungal infections > 2/year (y/n)`
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    group = case_when(
      `Fungal culture: C. albicans (y/n)` == "1" &
        `Symptom score (0-5)` >= 1 &
        `Recurring fungal infections > 2/year (y/n)` == "1" ~
        "RVVCpos",

      `Fungal culture: C. albicans (y/n)` == "0" &
        `Recurring fungal infections > 2/year (y/n)` == "1" ~
        "RVVCneg",

      `Fungal culture: C. albicans (y/n)` == "1" &
        `Symptom score (0-5)` == 0 ~
        "AS",

      `Fungal culture: C. albicans (y/n)` == "0" &
        `Recurring fungal infections > 2/year (y/n)` == "0" ~
        "Control",

      `Fungal culture: C. albicans (y/n)` == "1" &
        `Recurring fungal infections > 2/year (y/n)` == "0" ~
        "Candidapos",

      TRUE ~ NA_character_
    )
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    pos = case_when(
      `Fungal culture: C. albicans (y/n)` == "1" |
        `Fungal culture: Non-albicans candida spp. (y/n)` == 1 ~
        "pos",
      TRUE ~ "neg"
    ),
    .after = "group"
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    Clin_gr = g[as.character(.$`Clinical score (0-5)`)],
    .after = "group"
  ) %>%
  select("svamp_ID", group, everything())

taxa_col.fun <- function(df) {
  lvls <- names(pal_list)
  gr_lvls <- lvls %>% paste0(., collapse = "|")
  d <- df %>%
    mutate(
      gr_lvl = ifelse(
        str_detect(feature, gr_lvls),
        str_extract(feature, gr_lvls),
        "other"
      )
    ) %>%
    group_by(gr_lvl) %>%
    arrange(desc(abundance)) %>%
    select(gr_lvl, feature) %>%
    ungroup() %>%
    unique() %>%
    mutate(gr_lvl = factor(.$gr_lvl, levels = lvls)) %>%
    arrange(gr_lvl) %>%
    nest(.by = "gr_lvl") %>%
    mutate(
      data = map2(
        gr_lvl,
        data,
        ~ if (.x == "other") arrange(.y, as.character(feature)) else .y
      )
    ) %>%
    unnest(cols = c(data))

  col <- d %>%
    group_by(gr_lvl) %>%
    #mutate(col = list(pal_list[[cur_group_id()]])) %>%
    mutate(col = pal_list[[first(gr_lvl)]][seq_len(n())]) %>%
    ungroup() %>%
    select(-gr_lvl) %>%
    deframe()

  return(col)
}
Code 
############################
# GET CTRL SAMPLES #
###########################
t <- set_names(taxonomy, seq_along(taxonomy))
data_ctrl <- data %>%
  select(
    clade_name,
    contains("ex"),
    contains("seq"),
    contains("_run2"),
    starts_with("KX")
  ) %>% # removes ctrl and extra samples
  select(-matches("_1W|_3M|_6M")) %>%
  mutate(
    level = factor(
      t[as.character(str_count(clade_name, "\\|") + 1)],
      levels = taxonomy
    ),
    .after = "clade_name"
  ) # %>%
# separate(
#   col = clade_name,
#   into = taxonomy,
#   sep = "\\|",
#   remove = FALSE,
#   fill = "right"
# )

# Modify taxa labels
data_ctrl <- data_ctrl %>%
  mutate(
    taxa = str_extract_all(
      clade_name,
      "(?<=k__|p__|c__|o__|f__|g__|s__|t__)[^|]+"
    ),
    taxa = map2_chr(
      taxa,
      level,
      ~ {
        if (.y %in% c("species", "strain")) {
          # keep everything from genus onward
          start <- which(
            c("k", "p", "c", "o", "f", "g", "s", "t") %in% substr(.y, 1, 1)
          )
          paste(.x[start:length(.x)], collapse = " ")
        } else {
          # keep only the last element (current level)
          tail(.x, 1)
        }
      }
    ),
    .after = "level"
  ) %>%
  select(-clade_name) %>%
  rename(clade_name = taxa)

# pivot longer and calculate perecentage for the 15 most abundant taxa
df_ctrl_long <- data_ctrl %>%
  # select taxonomy level
  filter(grepl("strain", level)) %>%
  # remove long strain id, replace with int:
  # mutate(
  #   clade_name = make.unique(sub("\\s+\\S+$", "", clade_name), sep = " ")
  # ) %>%
  # mutate(strain = clade_name, .after = "level") %>%
  # replace "_" with " ":
  mutate(clade_name = str_replace_all(clade_name, "\\||_", " ")) %>%
  mutate(clade_name = str_replace(clade_name, " \\d", "")) %>%
  # removes taxa that sums to zero:
  filter(sum(c_across(where(is.double))) != 0) %>%
  # arrange acording to taxa rowsum
  arrange(desc(rowSums(across(where(is.numeric))))) %>%
  {
    . ->> top_taxa
  } %>%
  # mutate(clade_name = factor(.$clade_name, levels = .$clade_name)) %>%
  # slice_head(., n = 15) %>%
  pivot_longer(
    cols = where(is.double),
    names_to = "sample",
    values_to = "abundance"
  ) %>%
  # get genus-strain lvl columns:
  mutate(genus = str_extract(clade_name, "^\\w+"), .before = "sample") %>%
  mutate(
    species = str_replace(clade_name, " \\w+$", ""),
    .before = "sample"
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    strain = make.unique(sub("\\s+\\S+$", "", clade_name), sep = " "),
    .by = "sample",
    .before = "sample"
  )


#####################
# GET COLOUR PALLET #
#####################
# top taxa
# use this information to build a pallet for the 20 top abundant genus:
top_taxa <- df_ctrl_long %>%
  summarise(sum = sum(abundance), .by = c("genus", "species", "strain")) %>%
  arrange(desc(sum)) %>%
  # get right order of legend
  mutate(species = factor(.$species, levels = unique(.$species))) %>%
  mutate(genus = factor(.$genus, levels = unique(.$genus))) %>%
  arrange(genus, species, strain) %>%
  {
    . ->> top
  } %>%
  nest(., .by = "genus") %>%
  .[1:20, ]

# top 20 genus colour pallet
MG_colours <- df_ctrl_long %>%
  # Non-abundant taxa to "other":
  mutate(feature = strain) %>%
  mutate(
    feature = ifelse(
      grepl(paste0(top_taxa$genus, collapse = "|"), .$strain),
      .$strain,
      "other"
    )
  ) %>%
  # gets colour for each taxa
  taxa_col.fun(.)

# save pallet for later use
top %>%
  mutate(
    col = ifelse(strain %in% names(MG_colours), MG_colours[.$strain], "gray")
  ) #%>%

All the negative control samples were spiked with Alicyclobacillus acidiphilus, which is a known contaminant, and should therefore be removed from any other samples.

Step 3: Taxonomical-filtering

keep taxa with at least 0.005% in at least 6% (6 out of 93) of samples, or at least 2% relative abundance in at least 1 sample.

    .after = "clade_name"

# before taxa filtering we select the MOFA selected samples
m <- read_csv("../Results/Sample_omic_table.csv")
Rows: 96 Columns: 9
── Column specification ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
Delimiter: ","
chr (1): sample
dbl (1): n_views

ℹ Use `spec()` to retrieve the full column specification for this data.
ℹ Specify the column types or set `show_col_types = FALSE` to quiet this message.
data <- data %>%
  select(clade_name, level, any_of(m$sample[m$at_least_two & m$all_BL]))

n_samples <- select(data, starts_with("S")) %>% ncol() # number of good samples
n_samples
[1] 87
# keep taxa with at least 0.005% in at least 6% (5 out of 87) of samples, or at least 2% relative abundance in at least 1 sample.

# --- Step 1. split clade name into seperate columns
temp <- data %>%
  separate(
    col = clade_name,
    into = taxonomy,
    sep = "\\|",
    remove = FALSE,
    fill = "right"
  )

# --- Step 2. Identify the strains to remove
strains_to_remove <- temp %>%
  filter(level == "strain") %>%
  filter(
    species == "s__Alicyclobacillus_acidiphilus" | # remove species thought to be contaminant
      !(rowSums(across(where(is.double), ~ .x > 0.005)) >=
        round(0.06 * n_samples) |
        rowSums(across(where(is.double), ~ .x >= 2)) >= 1)
  )

# pander table of strains to remove
strains_to_remove %>%
  mutate(sum = rowSums(across(where(is.numeric))), .after = "level") %>%
  arrange(sum) %>%
  # keeps any row where at least one numeric column has a value greater than zero
  filter(if_any(where(is.double), ~ .x > 0)) %>%
  arrange(desc(sum)) %>%
  # removes samples with colsum = zero:
  select(
    -where(~ is.numeric(.x) && sum(.x) == 0)
  ) %>%
  select(species, strain, sum, matches("^S\\d\\d$")) %>%
  {
    . ->> tab
  } %>% # Colour only the sample columns
  mutate(
    .,
    across(
      3:ncol(.),
      ~ ifelse(
        .x > 0,
        paste0('<span style="color:red">', .x, '</span>'),
        .x
      )
    )
  ) %>%
  knitr::kable(
    digits = 1,
    caption = "Values larger than zero is coloured in red. 86 rows with rowsum = 0 was removed, as well as the 100 more strain level taxa seen bellow:",
    escape = FALSE
  )

  # pivot_longer(cols = where(is.double), names_to = "sample", values_to = "removed_abundance") %>%
  select(-level) %>%
  pivot_longer(
    cols = kingdom:strain,
    names_to = "level",

  ) %>%
  relocate(level, name, .before = "S01") %>%
  nest(.by = c(level)) %>%
  mutate(
    data = purrr::map(
      data,
      ~ summarise(.x, across(where(is.double), ~ sum(.)), .by = c("name"))
    )
  ) %>%
  mutate(data = setNames(.[["data"]], .$level))

# --- Step 4. get longer format and add back clade_names
# function to get clade name
get_full_clade.fun <- function(df) {
  # This will add a new column called match_clade
  # with the full clade_name that ends with the string from tissue_renorm_filt$clade_name
  df %>%
    mutate(
      match_clade = map_chr(
        name,
        ~ {
          hit <- data$clade_name[str_detect(
            data$clade_name,
            paste0(.x, "$")
          )]
          if (length(hit) > 0) hit[1] else NA_character_
        }
      )
    ) %>%
    select(match_clade) %>%
    pull()
}

removals <- removed_all_lvls %>%
  unnest(cols = data) %>%
  mutate(clade_name = get_full_clade.fun(.), .before = "level")

# --- Step 5. Subtract from higher levels
data_filt <- data %>%
  filter(
    !(level == "strain" & clade_name %in% strains_to_remove$clade_name)
  ) %>%
  # Join percentages to be subtracted
  left_join(
    select(removals, -name),
    by = c("level", "clade_name"),
    suffix = c("", "_rm")
  ) %>%
  relocate("S02_rm", .before = "S02") %>%
  # Subtract sample-wise values
  # coalesce handels the NA values introduced by left_join
  mutate(
    across(
      matches("^S\\d\\d$"),
      ~ if_else(
        level == "strain",
        .x,
        .x - coalesce(get(paste0(cur_column(), "_rm")), 0)
      )
    )
  ) %>%
  # removes now empty rows:
  filter(rowSums(across(matches("^S\\d\\d$")), na.rm = TRUE) != 0) %>%
  #filter(abs(rowSums(across(matches("^S\\d\\d$")), na.rm = TRUE)) > 1e-12) %>%
  select(-ends_with("_rm"))

# --- Step 7: check and replace negatives ---
indx <- which(data_filt < 0, arr.ind = TRUE)

if (nrow(indx) > 0) {
  neg_report <- tibble(
    neg = map2_dbl(indx[, 1], indx[, 2], ~ data_filt[[.x, .y]]),
    remove = map2_dbl(indx[, 1], indx[, 2], ~ data[[.x, .y]]), # original value from data
    col = map_chr(indx[, 2], ~ colnames(data)[.x]), # column name
    tax = map_chr(indx[, 1], ~ data[[.x, 1]]) # taxon/clade name
  )

  message("Negative values found and replaced with 0:")
  print(neg_report)

  # --- Step 7: replace negatives with zero ---
  data_filt <- data_filt %>%
    mutate(across(where(is.numeric), ~ pmax(.x, 0)))
}

Step 4: Simplify clade names

Now we want to simplify the clade_name column so that:

  • For phylum / class / order / family / genus, only the relevant level is kept.
  • For species and strain, all levels are incuded down from genus,
    i.e. "Genus species" or "Genus species strain".
# string manipulation

# data_filt_norm <- read_csv("../Results/Tissue_QC/Metageonome_all_vagswab_metaphlan_taxa_filt.csv")

# Modify taxa labels
data_filt_norm <- data_filt_norm %>%
  mutate(
    taxa = str_extract_all(
      clade_name,
      "(?<=k__|p__|c__|o__|f__|g__|s__|t__)[^|]+"
    ),
    taxa = map2_chr(
      taxa,
      level,
      ~ {
        if (.y %in% c("species", "strain")) {
          # keep everything from genus onward
          start <- which(
            c("k", "p", "c", "o", "f", "g", "s", "t") %in% substr(.y, 1, 1)
          )
          paste(.x[start:length(.x)], collapse = " ")
        } else {
          # keep only the last element (current level)
          tail(.x, 1)
        }
      }
    ),
    .after = "level"
  ) %>%
  select(-clade_name) %>%
  rename(clade_name = taxa)

# Section ####
# order samples by percentage of specified taxa based on assigned microbiome group
# NB! I found that I got a cleaner looking graph by using gardnerella also for L4 (typ = identity)
factor.fun <- function(df) {
  # title1 ----
  l <- c(
    "Lactobacillus" = "crispatus",
    "iners" = "iners",
    "Gardnerella" = "Gardnerella",
    "other" = "Gardnerella"
  )
  imap(
    l,
    ~ filter(df, gr == .y & str_detect(clade_name, .x)) %>%
      arrange(., desc(abundance)) %>%
      select(sample, gr) %>%
      unique() %>%
      pull(., "sample")
  ) %>%
    unlist()
}

    ) %>%
    mutate(
      gr = ifelse(
        str_detect(first(clade_name), "iners"),
        "iners",
        gr
      )
    ) %>%
    mutate(
      gr = ifelse(
        gr == "iners" &
          str_detect(nth(clade_name, n = 2), "crispatus"),
        "Lactobacillus",
        gr
      )
    ) %>%
    ungroup() %>%
    select(sample, gr) %>%
    unique() %>%
    deframe()
  return(groups)
}

taxa_order.fun <- function(df) {
  #lvls <- c("Lactobacillus", "Gardnerella", "Prevotella", "Bacillus", "other")
  lvls <- c(
    "Lactobacillus",
    "Gardnerella",
    "Prevotella",
    "Fannyhessea",
    "Sneathia",
    "other"
  )
  gr_lvls <- lvls %>% paste0(., collapse = "|")
  d <- df %>% # df_long_ %>%
    mutate(
      gr_lvl = ifelse(
        str_detect(clade_name, gr_lvls),
        str_extract(clade_name, gr_lvls),
        "other"
      )
    ) %>%
    group_by(gr_lvl) %>%
    arrange(desc(abundance)) %>%
    select(strain, gr_lvl, clade_name) %>%
    ungroup() %>%
    #unique() %>%
    mutate(gr_lvl = factor(.$gr_lvl, levels = lvls)) %>%
    arrange(gr_lvl) %>%
    nest(.by = "gr_lvl") %>%
    mutate(
      data = map2(
        gr_lvl,
        data,
        ~ if (.x == "other") arrange(.y, as.character(clade_name)) else .y
      )
    ) %>%
    unnest(cols = c(`data`))

  # add nested col pallet column
  # col <- d %>%
  #   group_by(gr_lvl) %>%
  #   mutate(col = pal_list[[cur_group_id()]][1:n()]) %>%
  #   ungroup() %>%
  #   select(-gr_lvl) %>%
  #   deframe()

  return(d$gr_lvl)
}

  mutate(

  ) %>%

  # removes taxa that sums to zero:
  filter(sum(c_across(where(is.double))) != 0) %>%
  # arrange acording to taxa rowsum

  # slice_head(., n = 15) %>%
  pivot_longer(
    cols = where(is.double),
    names_to = "sample",

  )

Step 6: Centered Log Ratio (CLR) Transformation

For technical, biological and computational reasons, microbiome data is compositional such that they represent proportions or relative information. Proportional data are restricted to a space where the sum of all OTU proportions for a given sample sums to 1. Using standard statistical methods on such data may lead to spurious results. Likewise, any data that are compositional in nature are interpreted into relative counts. Hence, using a CLR transformation allows the circumvention of these spurious results.

There are two ways of log-ratio transforming the data in mixOmics:

  • Option 1: Some of our functions (pca, plsda) directly include the argument logratio = ‘CLR’, so all you need to do is include your filtered offset data and add this argument (see example below).
  • Option 2: Some functions currently do not include the logratio argument. In this case, you will need to use the logratio.transfo() function as shown below. You can also use this function if you only have access to TSS (proportions) data and those were not offset.

unlike 16S data which are returned as raw counts after pre-processing, shotgun metageome data is often already normalized into proportions. This is because direct counts aren’t very meaningful across different taxa/genomes. That is why we will go with option 2 for our data.

information taken from: https://mixomics.org/mixmc/mixmc-preprocessing/

Shotgun metagenomics

  • You sequence all DNA in the sample, not just one marker gene.
  • Reads are mapped to reference genomes, genes, or functional categories.
  • Raw counts can be biased by factors like:
    • genome size
    • gene length
    • variable sequencing depth
  • Because of this, many sequencing facilities preprocess shotgun data to produce normalized relative abundances (proportions), so that samples can be compared more easily.

Typical outputs include:
- Relative abundance (%) of taxa
- RPKM / TPM / CPM for genes or functions

NB! the majority of mixOmics functions expect a format of samples as rows and features as columns, thus it is VERY important to first transpose the data when applying CLR!

# Create matrix for all levels of taxa and transpose to samples (rows) x taxa (columns)
matrix <- data_filt_norm %>%
  #rename_with(~ str_replace(.x, "_BL$", ""), everything()) %>%
  nest(data = -level) %>%
  # filter(level == "strain") %>%
  mutate(
    data = map(
      data,
      ~ .x %>%
        column_to_rownames(var = "clade_name") %>%
        as.matrix() %>%
        t()
    )
  )

matrix
# A tibble: 8 × 2
  level   data           
  <chr>   <list>         
1 kingdom <dbl [87 × 2]> 
2 phylum  <dbl [87 × 8]> 
3 class   <dbl [87 × 13]>
4 order   <dbl [87 × 16]>
5 family  <dbl [87 × 21]>
6 genus   <dbl [87 × 32]>
7 species <dbl [87 × 51]>
8 strain  <dbl [87 × 57]>
# Specify levels you want to process
tax_levels <- c("order", "family", "genus", "species", "strain")

matrix <- matrix %>%
  # Apply CLR transformation and PCA to each level
  mutate(
    # go from percent to proportion (sum to 1)
    data = map(data, ~ .x / 100),
    clr_data = map(
      data,
      ~ logratio.transfo(.x, logratio = "CLR", offset = 1e-6)
    )
  ) %>%
  mutate(across(2:3, ~ set_names(.x, paste0(.data[["level"]]))))

# check samples sum to 1 instead of 100
rowSums(matrix$data[[4]][1:3, ])

  saveRDS(

    "../Results/MixOmic/Metageonome_vagswab_CLR_transformed_1e-6.RDS"
  )

matrix <- matrix %>%
  # Filter matrix to only these levels
  filter(level %in% tax_levels) %>%

  # Apply CLR transformation and PCA to each level
  mutate(
    #clr_data = map(data, ~ logratio.transfo(.x, logratio = "CLR", offset = 1e-6)),
    pca_res = map(clr_data, ~ pca(.x)),
    plot = map2(
      pca_res,
      level,
      ~ plotIndiv(
        .x,
        col = pal$Clin_gr[1:length(unique(gr$Clin_gr))],
        group = gr$Clin_gr,
        ind.names = F,
        size.title = 9,
        title = paste0(.y)

    plot2 = map2(
      pca_res,
      level,
      ~ plotIndiv(
        .x,
        col = pal$RVVC_pos[1:length(unique(gr$RVVC_pos))],
        group = gr$RVVC_pos,
        ind.names = F,
        size.title = 9,
        title = paste0(.y)
      )
    )
  ) %>%
  mutate(across(2:5, ~ set_names(.x, paste0(.data[["level"]]))))

breaks.fun <- function(min, max, n) {
  x <- seq(min, max, length.out = n)
  x[which(x == median(x))] <- 0
  round(x)

}

## Overview: 
#### Quality Control and Normalization

1. **Step 1: Load data and meta data**  
   Load data and meta data and filter out any QC samples.  
2. **Step 2: Filter low count samples**  
   Inspect quality control samples by plotting
3. **Step 3: Taxonomical-filtering**  
   Identify treshold for low abundant taxa to filter<br>
    1. Split clade name into seperate columns<br>
    2. Identify the strains to remove<br>
    3. Aggregate removed strains by higher levels<br>
    4. Get longer format and add back clade_names<br>
    5. Subtract filtered taxa from each higher taxa levels<br>
    6. Check for samples with total taxa < 60% after filtering<br>
    7. Check and replace negative values with zero<br>
    8. Re-normalize each sample to 100%<br>
4. **Step 4: Simplify clade names**  
5. **Step 5: Plot barplots**  
5. **Step 6: Centered Log Ratio (CLR) Transformation**  
6. **Step 7: Exploratory Unsupervised PCA**  
7. **Step 8: Exploratory Heatmap**

```{r group-assignment}
#| code-fold: true
#| eval: false
g <- c(
  "0" = "0-1",
  "1" = "0-1",
  "2" = "2-3",
  "3" = "2-3",
  "4" = "4-5",
  "5" = "4-5"
)

gr_data <- meta_data %>%
  rename(
    `Symptom score (0-5)` = "Symptom score (0-5) - ibland har de svarat olika skriftligt i frågeformuläret och muntligt vid inklusiion, då har jag valt den högsta scoren"
  ) %>%
  select(
    svamp_ID,
    `Clinical score (0-5)`,
    `Fungal culture: C. albicans (y/n)`,
    `Fungal culture: Non-albicans candida spp. (y/n)`,
    `Symptom score (0-5)`,
    `Recurring fungal infections > 2/year (y/n)`
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    group = case_when(
      `Fungal culture: C. albicans (y/n)` == "1" &
        `Symptom score (0-5)` >= 1 &
        `Recurring fungal infections > 2/year (y/n)` == "1" ~
        "RVVCpos",

      `Fungal culture: C. albicans (y/n)` == "0" &
        `Recurring fungal infections > 2/year (y/n)` == "1" ~
        "RVVCneg",

      `Fungal culture: C. albicans (y/n)` == "1" &
        `Symptom score (0-5)` == 0 ~
        "AS",

      `Fungal culture: C. albicans (y/n)` == "0" &
        `Recurring fungal infections > 2/year (y/n)` == "0" ~
        "Control",

      `Fungal culture: C. albicans (y/n)` == "1" &
        `Recurring fungal infections > 2/year (y/n)` == "0" ~
        "Candidapos",

      TRUE ~ NA_character_
    )
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    pos = case_when(
      `Fungal culture: C. albicans (y/n)` == "1" |
        `Fungal culture: Non-albicans candida spp. (y/n)` == 1 ~
        "pos",
      TRUE ~ "neg"
    ),
    .after = "group"
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    Clin_gr = g[as.character(.$`Clinical score (0-5)`)],
    .after = "group"
  ) %>%
  select("svamp_ID", group, everything())
```

```{r colour-function}
taxa_col.fun <- function(df) {
  lvls <- names(pal_list)
  gr_lvls <- lvls %>% paste0(., collapse = "|")
  d <- df %>%
    mutate(
      gr_lvl = ifelse(
        str_detect(feature, gr_lvls),
        str_extract(feature, gr_lvls),
        "other"
      )
    ) %>%
    group_by(gr_lvl) %>%
    arrange(desc(abundance)) %>%
    select(gr_lvl, feature) %>%
    ungroup() %>%
    unique() %>%
    mutate(gr_lvl = factor(.$gr_lvl, levels = lvls)) %>%
    arrange(gr_lvl) %>%
    nest(.by = "gr_lvl") %>%
    mutate(
      data = map2(
        gr_lvl,
        data,
        ~ if (.x == "other") arrange(.y, as.character(feature)) else .y
      )
    ) %>%
    unnest(cols = c(data))

  col <- d %>%
    group_by(gr_lvl) %>%
    #mutate(col = list(pal_list[[cur_group_id()]])) %>%
    mutate(col = pal_list[[first(gr_lvl)]][seq_len(n())]) %>%
    ungroup() %>%
    select(-gr_lvl) %>%
    deframe()

  return(col)
}
```

```{r plot-control-samples}
#| fig-width: 10
#| fig-height: 8
#| code-fold: true
############################
# GET CTRL SAMPLES #
###########################
t <- set_names(taxonomy, seq_along(taxonomy))
data_ctrl <- data %>%
  select(
    clade_name,
    contains("ex"),
    contains("seq"),
    contains("_run2"),
    starts_with("KX")
  ) %>% # removes ctrl and extra samples
  select(-matches("_1W|_3M|_6M")) %>%
  mutate(
    level = factor(
      t[as.character(str_count(clade_name, "\\|") + 1)],
      levels = taxonomy
    ),
    .after = "clade_name"
  ) # %>%
# separate(
#   col = clade_name,
#   into = taxonomy,
#   sep = "\\|",
#   remove = FALSE,
#   fill = "right"
# )

# Modify taxa labels
data_ctrl <- data_ctrl %>%
  mutate(
    taxa = str_extract_all(
      clade_name,
      "(?<=k__|p__|c__|o__|f__|g__|s__|t__)[^|]+"
    ),
    taxa = map2_chr(
      taxa,
      level,
      ~ {
        if (.y %in% c("species", "strain")) {
          # keep everything from genus onward
          start <- which(
            c("k", "p", "c", "o", "f", "g", "s", "t") %in% substr(.y, 1, 1)
          )
          paste(.x[start:length(.x)], collapse = " ")
        } else {
          # keep only the last element (current level)
          tail(.x, 1)
        }
      }
    ),
    .after = "level"
  ) %>%
  select(-clade_name) %>%
  rename(clade_name = taxa)

# pivot longer and calculate perecentage for the 15 most abundant taxa
df_ctrl_long <- data_ctrl %>%
  # select taxonomy level
  filter(grepl("strain", level)) %>%
  # remove long strain id, replace with int:
  # mutate(
  #   clade_name = make.unique(sub("\\s+\\S+$", "", clade_name), sep = " ")
  # ) %>%
  # mutate(strain = clade_name, .after = "level") %>%
  # replace "_" with " ":
  mutate(clade_name = str_replace_all(clade_name, "\\||_", " ")) %>%
  mutate(clade_name = str_replace(clade_name, " \\d", "")) %>%
  # removes taxa that sums to zero:
  filter(sum(c_across(where(is.double))) != 0) %>%
  # arrange acording to taxa rowsum
  arrange(desc(rowSums(across(where(is.numeric))))) %>%
  {
    . ->> top_taxa
  } %>%
  # mutate(clade_name = factor(.$clade_name, levels = .$clade_name)) %>%
  # slice_head(., n = 15) %>%
  pivot_longer(
    cols = where(is.double),
    names_to = "sample",
    values_to = "abundance"
  ) %>%
  # get genus-strain lvl columns:
  mutate(genus = str_extract(clade_name, "^\\w+"), .before = "sample") %>%
  mutate(
    species = str_replace(clade_name, " \\w+$", ""),
    .before = "sample"
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    strain = make.unique(sub("\\s+\\S+$", "", clade_name), sep = " "),
    .by = "sample",
    .before = "sample"
  )


#####################
# GET COLOUR PALLET #
#####################
# top taxa
# use this information to build a pallet for the 20 top abundant genus:
top_taxa <- df_ctrl_long %>%
  summarise(sum = sum(abundance), .by = c("genus", "species", "strain")) %>%
  arrange(desc(sum)) %>%
  # get right order of legend
  mutate(species = factor(.$species, levels = unique(.$species))) %>%
  mutate(genus = factor(.$genus, levels = unique(.$genus))) %>%
  arrange(genus, species, strain) %>%
  {
    . ->> top
  } %>%
  nest(., .by = "genus") %>%
  .[1:20, ]

# top 20 genus colour pallet
MG_colours <- df_ctrl_long %>%
  # Non-abundant taxa to "other":
  mutate(feature = strain) %>%
  mutate(
    feature = ifelse(
      grepl(paste0(top_taxa$genus, collapse = "|"), .$strain),
      .$strain,
      "other"
    )
  ) %>%
  # gets colour for each taxa
  taxa_col.fun(.)

# save pallet for later use
top %>%
  mutate(
    col = ifelse(strain %in% names(MG_colours), MG_colours[.$strain], "gray")
  ) #%>%
#write_csv(., "../Results/Metagenomics/Metagenome_col_pal.csv")

# Select top 20 species
# you can choose if you want to include species by sum abundance or by alfabetical
# dpending on if you use the levels() or just the order of n
n <- levels(top$species)
n_lvl <- top$species %>% unique() %>% as.vector()

#plot the ctrls
# quartz(width = 10, height = 8, dpi = 120)
barplot <- df_ctrl_long %>%
  #mutate(species = factor(species, levels = n)) %>%
  ggplot(
    .,
    aes(x = sample, y = abundance, fill = species) # round(value, digits = 3)
  ) +
  geom_col(width = .9, position = "stack") +
  # geom_text(aes(label = value), position = position_stack(vjust = 0.5)) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = MG_colours) + # pal[1:colourCount]
  guides(
    fill = guide_legend(
      override.aes = list(size = 2),
      ncol = 5,
      byrow = FALSE,
      keyheight = .4,
      keywidth = .6
    )
  ) +
  theme_classic() +
  coord_cartesian(expand = F) +
  theme(
    plot.margin = unit(c(1, 0.5, 1, 0), "cm"),
    legend.spacing.y = unit(.5, 'cm'),
    legend.title = element_blank(),
    legend.text = element_text(margin = margin(r = .3, l = .3, unit = "pt"), ),
    axis.title = element_blank(),
    axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 90, hjust = 1),
    legend.position = "bottom"
  )
barplot
```

All the negative control samples were spiked with Alicyclobacillus acidiphilus, which is a known contaminant, and should therefore be removed from any other samples.

## Step 3: Taxonomical-filtering
keep taxa with at least 0.005% in at least 6% (6 out of 93) of samples, or at least 2% relative abundance in at least 1 sample.

```{r filter-taxa}
# final
############################
# IDENTIFY TAXA TO FILTER #
###########################
t <- set_names(taxonomy, seq_along(taxonomy))
data <- data %>%
  select(
    -contains("ex"),
    -contains("seq"),
    -contains("_run2"),
    -starts_with("KX")
  ) %>% # removes ctrl and extra samples
  #select(-matches("_1W|_3M|_6M")) %>%
  mutate(
    level = factor(
      t[as.character(str_count(clade_name, "\\|") + 1)],
      levels = taxonomy
    ),
    .after = "clade_name"
  )

n_samples <- select(data, starts_with("S")) %>% ncol() # number of good samples
n_samples

# before taxa filtering we select the MOFA selected samples
m <- read_csv("../Results/Sample_omic_table.csv")
data <- data %>%
  select(clade_name, level, any_of(m$sample[m$at_least_two & m$all_BL]))

n_samples <- select(data, starts_with("S")) %>% ncol() # number of good samples
n_samples

# keep taxa with at least 0.005% in at least 6% (5 out of 87) of samples, or at least 2% relative abundance in at least 1 sample.

# --- Step 1. split clade name into seperate columns
temp <- data %>%
  separate(
    col = clade_name,
    into = taxonomy,
    sep = "\\|",
    remove = FALSE,
    fill = "right"
  )

# --- Step 2. Identify the strains to remove
strains_to_remove <- temp %>%
  filter(level == "strain") %>%
  filter(
    species == "s__Alicyclobacillus_acidiphilus" | # remove species thought to be contaminant
      !(rowSums(across(where(is.double), ~ .x > 0.005)) >=
        round(0.06 * n_samples) |
        rowSums(across(where(is.double), ~ .x >= 2)) >= 1)
  )

# pander table of strains to remove
strains_to_remove %>%
  mutate(sum = rowSums(across(where(is.numeric))), .after = "level") %>%
  arrange(sum) %>%
  # keeps any row where at least one numeric column has a value greater than zero
  filter(if_any(where(is.double), ~ .x > 0)) %>%
  arrange(desc(sum)) %>%
  # removes samples with colsum = zero:
  select(
    -where(~ is.numeric(.x) && sum(.x) == 0)
  ) %>%
  select(species, strain, sum, matches("^S\\d\\d$")) %>%
  {
    . ->> tab
  } %>% # Colour only the sample columns
  mutate(
    .,
    across(
      3:ncol(.),
      ~ ifelse(
        .x > 0,
        paste0('<span style="color:red">', .x, '</span>'),
        .x
      )
    )
  ) %>%
  knitr::kable(
    digits = 1,
    caption = "Values larger than zero is coloured in red. 86 rows with rowsum = 0 was removed, as well as the 100 more strain level taxa seen bellow:",
    escape = FALSE
  )
# samples that had no taxa removed are not included in this table
# thats why there are 60 columns
dim(tab)

# --- Step 3. Aggregate removed strains by higher levels
removed_all_lvls <- strains_to_remove %>%
  # pivot_longer(cols = where(is.double), names_to = "sample", values_to = "removed_abundance") %>%
  select(-level) %>%
  pivot_longer(
    cols = kingdom:strain,
    names_to = "level",
    values_to = "name"
  ) %>%
  relocate(level, name, .before = "S01") %>%
  nest(.by = c(level)) %>%
  mutate(
    data = purrr::map(
      data,
      ~ summarise(.x, across(where(is.double), ~ sum(.)), .by = c("name"))
    )
  ) %>%
  mutate(data = setNames(.[["data"]], .$level))

removed_all_lvls

knitr::kable(removed_all_lvls$data[[2]], digits = 1)


# --- Step 4. get longer format and add back clade_names
# function to get clade name
get_full_clade.fun <- function(df) {
  # This will add a new column called match_clade
  # with the full clade_name that ends with the string from tissue_renorm_filt$clade_name
  df %>%
    mutate(
      match_clade = map_chr(
        name,
        ~ {
          hit <- data$clade_name[str_detect(
            data$clade_name,
            paste0(.x, "$")
          )]
          if (length(hit) > 0) hit[1] else NA_character_
        }
      )
    ) %>%
    select(match_clade) %>%
    pull()
}

removals <- removed_all_lvls %>%
  unnest(cols = data) %>%
  mutate(clade_name = get_full_clade.fun(.), .before = "level")

# removals %>% filter(level == "strain")

#############################
# FILTER AT ALL TAXA LEVELS #
############################
# --- Step 5. Subtract from higher levels
data_filt <- data %>%
  filter(
    !(level == "strain" & clade_name %in% strains_to_remove$clade_name)
  ) %>%
  # Join percentages to be subtracted
  left_join(
    select(removals, -name),
    by = c("level", "clade_name"),
    suffix = c("", "_rm")
  ) %>%
  relocate("S02_rm", .before = "S02") %>%
  # Subtract sample-wise values
  # coalesce handels the NA values introduced by left_join
  mutate(
    across(
      matches("^S\\d\\d$"),
      ~ if_else(
        level == "strain",
        .x,
        .x - coalesce(get(paste0(cur_column(), "_rm")), 0)
      )
    )
  ) %>%
  # removes now empty rows:
  filter(rowSums(across(matches("^S\\d\\d$")), na.rm = TRUE) != 0) %>%
  #filter(abs(rowSums(across(matches("^S\\d\\d$")), na.rm = TRUE)) > 1e-12) %>%
  select(-ends_with("_rm"))

data %>%
  nest(.by = c(level))
data_filt %>%

if (nrow(indx) > 0) {
```

## Step 4: Simplify clade names

Now we want to simplify the `clade_name` column so that:

- For **phylum / class / order / family / genus**, only the relevant level is kept.
- For **species** and **strain**, all levels are incuded down from genus,  
  i.e. `"Genus species"` or `"Genus species strain"`.
  
```{r simplify-clade_name}
# string manipulation

# data_filt_norm <- read_csv("../Results/Tissue_QC/Metageonome_all_vagswab_metaphlan_taxa_filt.csv")

# Modify taxa labels
data_filt_norm <- data_filt_norm %>%
  mutate(
    taxa = str_extract_all(
      clade_name,
      "(?<=k__|p__|c__|o__|f__|g__|s__|t__)[^|]+"
    ),
    taxa = map2_chr(
      taxa,
      level,
      ~ {
        if (.y %in% c("species", "strain")) {
          # keep everything from genus onward
          start <- which(
            c("k", "p", "c", "o", "f", "g", "s", "t") %in% substr(.y, 1, 1)
          )
          paste(.x[start:length(.x)], collapse = " ")
        } else {
          # keep only the last element (current level)
          tail(.x, 1)
        }
      }
    ),
    .after = "level"
  ) %>%
  select(-clade_name) %>%
  rename(clade_name = taxa)
```

```{r helper-functions-for-plotting}
#| code-fold: true
# Section ####
# order samples by percentage of specified taxa based on assigned microbiome group
# NB! I found that I got a cleaner looking graph by using gardnerella also for L4 (typ = identity)
factor.fun <- function(df) {
  # title1 ----
  l <- c(
    "Lactobacillus" = "crispatus",
    "iners" = "iners",
    "Gardnerella" = "Gardnerella",
    "other" = "Gardnerella"
  )
  imap(
    l,
    ~ filter(df, gr == .y & str_detect(clade_name, .x)) %>%
      arrange(., desc(abundance)) %>%
      select(sample, gr) %>%
      unique() %>%
      pull(., "sample")
  ) %>%
    unlist()
}
gr.fun <- function(df) {
  # clean up the clade_name column
  # df <- df %>%
  #   group_by(sample) %>%
  #   arrange(desc(clade_name)) %>%
  #   mutate(clade_name = str_replace_all(clade_name, "\\w__", "")) %>%
  #   mutate(clade_name = str_replace_all(clade_name, "\\||_", " ")) %>%
  #   ungroup()

  groups <- df %>% # df_long_ %>%
    group_by(sample) %>%
    arrange(desc(abundance)) %>%
    mutate(gr = clade_name[which.max(abundance)]) %>%
    mutate(gr = str_extract(first(gr), "^\\w+")) %>%
    mutate(
      gr = case_when(
        str_detect(gr, "Lactobacillus|Gardnerella") ~ gr,
        TRUE ~ "other"
      )
    ) %>%
    mutate(
      gr = ifelse(
        str_detect(first(clade_name), "iners"),
        "iners",
        gr
      )
    ) %>%
    mutate(
      gr = ifelse(
        gr == "iners" &
          str_detect(nth(clade_name, n = 2), "crispatus"),
        "Lactobacillus",
        gr
      )
    ) %>%
    ungroup() %>%
    select(sample, gr) %>%
    unique() %>%
    deframe()
  return(groups)
}

taxa_order.fun <- function(df) {
  #lvls <- c("Lactobacillus", "Gardnerella", "Prevotella", "Bacillus", "other")
  lvls <- c(
    "Lactobacillus",
    "Gardnerella",
    "Prevotella",
    "Fannyhessea",
    "Sneathia",
    "other"
  )
  gr_lvls <- lvls %>% paste0(., collapse = "|")
  d <- df %>% # df_long_ %>%
    mutate(
      gr_lvl = ifelse(
        str_detect(clade_name, gr_lvls),
        str_extract(clade_name, gr_lvls),
        "other"
      )
    ) %>%
    group_by(gr_lvl) %>%
    arrange(desc(abundance)) %>%
    select(strain, gr_lvl, clade_name) %>%
    ungroup() %>%
    #unique() %>%
    mutate(gr_lvl = factor(.$gr_lvl, levels = lvls)) %>%
    arrange(gr_lvl) %>%
    nest(.by = "gr_lvl") %>%
    mutate(
      data = map2(
        gr_lvl,
        data,
        ~ if (.x == "other") arrange(.y, as.character(clade_name)) else .y
      )
    ) %>%
    unnest(cols = c(`data`))

  # add nested col pallet column
  # col <- d %>%
  #   group_by(gr_lvl) %>%
  #   mutate(col = pal_list[[cur_group_id()]][1:n()]) %>%
  #   ungroup() %>%
  #   select(-gr_lvl) %>%
  #   deframe()

  return(d$gr_lvl)
}
```

## Step 6: Centered Log Ratio (CLR) Transformation
For technical, biological and computational reasons, microbiome data is compositional such that they represent proportions or relative information. Proportional data are restricted to a space where the sum of all OTU proportions for a given sample sums to 1. Using standard statistical methods on such data may lead to spurious results. Likewise, any data that are compositional in nature are interpreted into relative counts. Hence, using a CLR transformation allows the circumvention of these spurious results.

There are two ways of log-ratio transforming the data in mixOmics:

  - Option 1: Some of our functions (pca, plsda) directly include the argument logratio = 'CLR', so all you need to do is include your filtered offset data and add this argument (see example below).
  - Option 2: Some functions currently do not include the logratio argument. In this case, you will need to use the logratio.transfo() function as shown below. You can also use this function if you only have access to TSS (proportions) data and those were not offset.

unlike 16S data which are returned as raw counts after pre-processing, shotgun metageome data is often already normalized into proportions. This is because direct counts aren’t very meaningful across different taxa/genomes. That is why we will go with option 2 for our data.

information taken from:
https://mixomics.org/mixmc/mixmc-preprocessing/

### Shotgun metagenomics

- You sequence **all DNA** in the sample, not just one marker gene.  
- Reads are mapped to **reference genomes, genes, or functional categories**.  
- Raw counts can be biased by factors like:
  - genome size  
  - gene length  
  - variable sequencing depth  
- Because of this, many sequencing facilities preprocess shotgun data to produce **normalized relative abundances (proportions)**, so that samples can be compared more easily.  

**Typical outputs include:**  
- Relative abundance (%) of taxa  
- RPKM / TPM / CPM for genes or functions 

**NB!** the majority of mixOmics functions expect a format of samples as rows and features as columns, thus it is 
VERY important to first transpose the data when applying CLR!
```{r normalize}
# Create matrix for all levels of taxa and transpose to samples (rows) x taxa (columns)
matrix <- data_filt_norm %>%
  #rename_with(~ str_replace(.x, "_BL$", ""), everything()) %>%
  nest(data = -level) %>%
  # filter(level == "strain") %>%
  mutate(
    data = map(
      data,
      ~ .x %>%
        column_to_rownames(var = "clade_name") %>%
        as.matrix() %>%
        t()
    )
  )

matrix

# Specify levels you want to process
tax_levels <- c("order", "family", "genus", "species", "strain")

matrix <- matrix %>%
  # Apply CLR transformation and PCA to each level
  mutate(
    # go from percent to proportion (sum to 1)
    data = map(data, ~ .x / 100),
    clr_data = map(
      data,
      ~ logratio.transfo(.x, logratio = "CLR", offset = 1e-6)
    )
  ) %>%
  mutate(across(2:3, ~ set_names(.x, paste0(.data[["level"]]))))

# check samples sum to 1 instead of 100
rowSums(matrix$data[[4]][1:3, ])
```

```{r save-CLR-transformed-data}
matrix %>%
  select(1, data, clr_data) %>%
  saveRDS(
    .,
    "../Results/MixOmic/Metageonome_vagswab_CLR_transformed_1e-6.RDS"
  )
```

## Step 7: Exploratory Unsupervised PCA

```{r get-new-groups}
gr <- tibble(ID = colnames(data)[-c(1, 2)]) %>%
  #left_join(., gr_data, by = c("ID" = "svamp_ID"))
  left_join(., meta_gr, by = c("ID" = "sample"))

# gr <- tibble(sample = colnames(data)[-c(1, 2)]) %>%
#   left_join(., meta_gr, by = "sample")
```


```{r plot-PCA}
#| output: false
matrix <- matrix %>%
  # Filter matrix to only these levels
  filter(level %in% tax_levels) %>%

  # Apply CLR transformation and PCA to each level
  mutate(
    #clr_data = map(data, ~ logratio.transfo(.x, logratio = "CLR", offset = 1e-6)),
    pca_res = map(clr_data, ~ pca(.x)),
    plot = map2(
      pca_res,
      level,
      ~ plotIndiv(
        .x,
        col = pal$Clin_gr[1:length(unique(gr$Clin_gr))],
        group = gr$Clin_gr,
        ind.names = F,
        size.title = 9,
        title = paste0(.y)
      )
    ),
    plot2 = map2(
      pca_res,
      level,
      ~ plotIndiv(
        .x,
        col = pal$RVVC_pos[1:length(unique(gr$RVVC_pos))],
        group = gr$RVVC_pos,
        ind.names = F,
        size.title = 9,
        title = paste0(.y)
      )
    )
  ) %>%
  mutate(across(2:5, ~ set_names(.x, paste0(.data[["level"]]))))

# Plot PCA for selected levels
l <- get_legend(
  plotIndiv(
    matrix$pca_res[["genus"]],
    col = pal$Clin_gr[1:length(unique(gr$Clin_gr))],
    legend = T,
    group = gr$Clin_gr
  )$graph
)
l2 <- get_legend(
  plotIndiv(
    matrix$pca_res[["genus"]],
    col = pal$RVVC_pos[1:length(unique(gr$RVVC_pos))],
    legend = T,
    group = gr$RVVC_pos
  )$graph
)
p <- matrix$plot %>% map("graph")
p2 <- matrix$plot2 %>% map("graph")
```

```{r plot-panels}

plot_grid(
```

Now that the data is:

- filtered for low abundant taxa  
- CLR transformed  
- offset added

## Step 8: Exploratory Heatmap

```{r heatmap-matrix}
library(ComplexHeatmap)
library(circlize)

# no need to scale or center abundance data as this inherently in percent:
# we only need to log transforme the data and add a off-set
# I dont know if it is more appropriate to use abundanc or CLR normalized data

# CLR
matrix.h <- matrix$clr_data$species %>% t()

# log abundance
# matrix.h <- matrix.h + 0.0001 %>% log2()

# Filter
matrix.h <- matrix.h[, gr$ID]

top <- sort(rowSums(t(matrix$data$species)), decreasing = T)[1:50]
matrix.h <- matrix.h[names(top), ]

dim(matrix.h)
```

```{r heatmap-annotation}
##############
# ANNOTATION #
##############
# colour pallets
blue <- brewer.pal(6, name = "Blues")
purple <- brewer.pal(6, name = "Purples")
reds <- brewer.pal(6, name = "Reds")

Red <- brewer.pal(6, name = "Reds") %>% c(., "gray")
pal1 <- c("#f26386", "#a4d984", "#fbbc52") %>% c(., "gray") # "#f588af", "#fd814e"
pal2 <- c("#2266ac", "#91c5de") %>% c(., "gray")
pal3 <- c("#9e8dec", "#902267", "#cc93cf", "#a5c97b", "#de9548") %>%
  c(., "gray") #"#abcb4b" "#63d3b4"


# group information
cols <- c(
  "Clin_gr",
  "RVVC_pos",
  "Clinical score (0-5)",
  "Fungal culture: C. albicans (y/n)"
) %>%
  set_names()
# use if there are NAs:
lvls <- map(cols, ~ c(sort(unique(gr[[.x]])), "na"))

annot_df <- gr %>%
  select(1, any_of(cols)) %>%
  mutate(across(2:ncol(.), ~ factor(.x))) %>%
  # when NAs are present:
  #mutate(across(all_of(cols), ~ factor(.x, levels = lvls[[cur_column()]]))) %>%
  column_to_rownames(var = "ID")

# order samples acording to matrix
annot_df <- annot_df[colnames(matrix.h), ]

ann_colors <- map(colnames(annot_df), function(val) {
  # Levels for this column
  levs <- levels(annot_df[[val]])

  # CASE 1: column exists in pal → use provided palette
  if (val %in% names(pal)) {
    colors <- pal[[val]]
    return(set_names(colors[1:length(levs)], levs))
  }
  # CASE 2: column not in pal → generate paired palette
  colors <- gg_color_hue(length(levs))
  set_names(colors, levs)
  # colors <- brewer.pal(length(levs), "Paired")
  # if (length(levs) == length(colors)) {
  #   set_names(colors, levs)
  # } else {
  #   set_names(colors[1:length(levs)], levs)
  # }
})
# Name the list by column names
ann_colors <- set_names(ann_colors, colnames(annot_df))

# check samples number
dim(matrix.h)
dim(annot_df)

# top annotation object:
top_annot <- columnAnnotation(
  df = annot_df,
  #show_legend = FALSE,
  show_annotation_name = T,
  annotation_name_gp = gpar(fontsize = 8),
  annotation_legend_param = list(
    grid_height = unit(.1, "mm"),
    grid_width = unit(2, "mm"),
    title = "",
    labels_gp = gpar(fontsize = 7),
    title_gp = gpar(fontsize = 8)
  ),
  simple_anno_size = unit(.3, "cm"),
  #gap = unit(1, "cm"),
  col = ann_colors
)
```

```{r heatmap-color-scale}
#| fig-cap: "Figure 3: Histogram showing the distribution of CLR normalized matrix values"

################
# PLOT HEATMAP #

# colour mapping
breaks.fun <- function(min, max, n) {
  x <- seq(min, max, length.out = n)
  x[which(x == median(x))] <- 0
  round(x)
  return(x)
}

q <- quantile(matrix.h, probs = seq(0, 1, 0.1))
```
